observations.seen: Frame 1 is labeled 'Golden Hour Look' but renders as a murky purple dusk with flat fill and no readable key direction. Frame 3 has a convincing low warm sun, so the lighting presets are inconsistent in quality.

Frame 3 shadows have heavy stair-step aliasing along the bleacher and left court edges. Frame 2 shows dark rectangular patches on the floor that read as broken blob shadows. In frame 1 the players have almost no contact shadow under their feet.
Only frame 4 shows meaningful reflection: a blue specular streak and lamp glints on the wet-looking court. The other frames have matte surfaces with little environment response.

The buildings in frames 1 and 3 are flat boxes with a uniform grid of emissive window squares. The bleachers are plain untextured steps. The blue tower in frame 4 has a smeared, stretched texture, and the ornate lamps are the only detailed set dressing.
Frame 2 has indoor bloom and haze, but the depth of field blurs the gym into an unreadable smear. Frame 3's sky is blown out to white behind the buildings. Frame 4 has faint rain specks.
Clothing and skin use flat albedo with no fabric or skin response. The court reads as matte plastic in frames 1 to 3. The floor glyph in the bottom left of frames 2 and 4 is pixelated.
The characters are low-poly with near-identical faces and white goggle-like eyes. White curved arc artifacts protrude from players' ankles in every frame. The ball cart and backboard are reasonable.
Frame 1 crops a player at the left edge and the ball at the right edge, and the HUD panel covers players. Frames 2 to 4 cut off the hoop at the top right and a player at the right edge.

The camera is a low perspective at roughly 20 to 30 degrees of elevation, not the specified 70-degree orthographic broadcast view. Frame 1 sits so close that the court becomes a fragment rather than the 25 to 40 percent subject.
Grain, vignette, bloom and DOF are present. The DOF in frame 2 is overdone and frame 3 clips its highlights.
Most players stand in stiff A-poses with arms straight down. Only the dribbler shows a dynamic crouch.
The frame 1 scoreboard, stamina bar and control strip share a consistent style. The top mode and court bar is a dense developer-style menu, and the score panel overlaps gameplay.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
